That type of flue-cured tobacco commonly known as Foreign-grown Flue-cured, produced in countries other than the United States.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1075 — Undried.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The condition of unfermented tobacco which has not been air-dried or steam-dried.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1076 — Uniformity.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). An element of quality which describes the consistency of a lot of tobacco as it is prepared for market. Uniformity is expressed as a percentage in grade specifications. (See Rule 13.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1078 — Unstemmed.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A form of tobacco, including whole leaf and leaf scrap, from which the stems or midribs have not been removed.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1079 — Variegated (K).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any tobacco that does not blend with the normal colors of the types; any leaf of which 20 percent or more of its surface is grayish, mottled, bleached, doty-faced, scalded, or sunbaked. (See Rule 15.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1080 — Variegated dark red (KD).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A dark brownish-red discoloration which usually results from excessive sunbaking during the growing process or from storing cured tobacco over extended periods of time. Any leaf of which 20 percent or more of its surface is dark brownish-red may be described as variegated dark.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1081 — Variegated red or scorched (KR).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A red discoloration which usually results from excessive heat in the curing process. Any leaf of which 20 percent or more of its surface has been reddened in the curing process may be described as variegated red or scorched. (See Rule 16.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1082 — Waste.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The portion or portions of the web of tobacco leaves which have been lost or rendered less serviceable for use in tobacco products, including: (a) Portions which have decomposed or largely decomposed by field diseases and field-firing, pole-burning, bulk-burning; (b) portions which are dead.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1083 — Wet (W).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any sound tobacco containing excessive moisture to the extent that it is in unsafe or doubtful-keeping order. Wet applies to any tobacco which is not damaged but which is likely to damage if treated in the customary manner. (See Rule 22.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1084 — Whitish-lemon (LL).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A whitish-yellow color which usually results during wet growing seasons when rain leaches or washes out the yellow color from the leaf. Any leaf of which 20 percent or more of its leaf surface has whitish-yellow color may be described as whitish-lemon.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1085 — Width.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The relative breadth of a tobacco leaf expressed in relation to its length. Width, as an element of quality, does not apply to tobacco in strip form. (See Elements of Quality Chart.).

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). These standardized words or terms are used to describe tobacco quality and to assist in interpreting grade specifications. Tobacco attributes or characteristics which constitute quality are designated as elements of quality. The range within each element is expressed by the use of words or.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The application of these official standard grades shall be in accordance with the following rules.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1107 — Rule 1.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Each grade shall be treated as a subdivision of a particular type. When the grade is stated in an inspection certificate, the type also shall be stated.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1108 — Rule 2.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The determination of a grade shall be based upon a thorough examination of a lot of tobacco or of an official sample of the lot.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1109 — Rule 3.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). In drawing an official sample from a hogshead or other package of tobacco, three or more breaks shall be made at such points and in such manner as the inspector or sampler may find necessary to determine the kinds of tobacco and the percentage.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1110 — Rule 4.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). All standard grades must be clean unless otherwise noted by a special factor.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1111 — Rule 5.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The grade assigned to any lot of tobacco shall be a true representation of the tobacco at the time of inspection and certification. If, at any time, it is found that a lot of tobacco does not comply with the specifications of the grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1112 — Rule 6.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A lot of tobacco on the marginal line between two colors shall be placed in the color with which it best corresponds with respect to body or other associated elements of quality.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1113 — Rule 7.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of tobacco which meets the specifications of two grades shall be placed in the higher grade. Any lot of tobacco on the marginal line between two grades shall be placed in the lower grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1114 — Rule 8.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A lot of tobacco meets the specifications of a grade when it is not lower in any degree of any element of quality than the minimum specifications of such grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1115 — Rule 9.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The use of any grade may be restricted by the Director during any marketing season when it is found that the grade is not needed or appears in insufficient volume to justify its use.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1116 — Rule 10.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any special factor approved by the Director of the Tobacco Division, Agricultural Marketing Service, may be used to show a peculiar side or characteristic of the tobacco which tends to modify the grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1117 — Rule 11.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Interpretations, the use of specifications, and the meaning of terms shall be in accordance with determinations or clarifications made by the Chief of the Marketing Programs Branch and approved by the Director.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1118 — Rule 12.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). In determining the grade of a lot of tobacco, the lot as a whole shall be considered. Minor irregularities which do not affect over one percent of the tobacco shall be overlooked.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1119 — Rule 13.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Degrees of uniformity shall be expressed in terms of percentages. The percentages shall govern the portion of a lot which must meet the specifications of the grade. (These percentages shall not affect limitations established by other rules.) The minor portion must be closely related.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1120 — Rule 14.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The application of injury tolerance as an element of quality shall be expressed in terms of a percentage. The appraisal of injury shall be based upon the percentage of affected leaf surface or the degree of injury. In appraising injury, consideration shall be given.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1121 — Rule 15.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of tobacco containing 20 percent or more of variegated tobacco other than variegated red or scorched shall be described as variegated and designated by the color symbol “K,” “KL,” “KF,” “KD,” or “KV.”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1122 — Rule 16.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of ripe tobacco which contains 20 percent or more of variegated red or scorched tobacco shall be designated by the color symbol “KR.” Any lot of unripe tobacco which is under 20 percent greenish or green but which contains 20 percent or.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1123 — Rule 17.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of lemon, or orange colored tobacco containing over 20 percent of slick tobacco shall be designated by the symbol “S” in the X, C, or B groups.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1124 — Rule 18.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of mature tobacco in lemon or orange color containing 20 percent or more of greenish tobacco, or any lot which is not green but which contains 20 percent or more of greenish and green tobacco combined shall be designated by the color.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1125 — Rule 19.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Any lot of tobacco containing 20 percent or more of green tobacco, or any lot which is not crude but contains 20 percent or more of green and crude combined shall be designated by the color symbols “G,” “GR,” “GK,” “GG,” or the combination.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1126 — Rule 20.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Crude tobacco shall not be included in any grade of any color except green, green red, green variegated, gray green, or the combination symbols “GL,” or “GF” in the nondescript group. Any lot containing 20 percent or more of crude tobacco shall be classified.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1127 — Rule 21.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Damaged tobacco which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a special factor grade by placing the special factor “U” after the grademark.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1128 — Rule 22.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Sound tobacco that is wet or in doubtful-keeping order but which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a special factor grade by placing the special factor “W” after the grademark.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1129 — Rule 23.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Tobacco shall be designated by the grademark, “No-G-F,” when it contains stalks, suckers, or foreign matter such as straw, strings, rubber bands, grass, weeds, or an excessive amount of dirt or sand.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1131 — Rule 25.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Any lot of tobacco containing 10 percent or less of oxidized tobacco, except as provided in rule 12, shall be designated by the combination symbols “PO,” “XO,” or “BO.” Crude or green tobacco containing 10 percent or less of oxidized shall be grade “N2.”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1132 — Rule 26.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Tobacco that contains a moderate amount of dirt or sand, but which otherwise meets the specifications of any Primings grade, including the first quality Nondescript from the Primings group, shall be designated by placing the special factor, “dirt” or “sand” after the grademark.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1133 — Rule 27.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1134 — Rule 28.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco in strip form which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a special factor grade by placing the special factor “S” preceding the grademark.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1135 — Rule 29.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1162 — Leaf (B Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Leaves of the B group have a pointed tip, tend to fold, usually are heavier in body than the other groups, and show little or no ground injury.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1163 — Smoking Leaf (H Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves normally grown at or above the midportion of the stalk. Leaves of the H group show a high degree of maturity, more open leaf structure in relation to the B Group, and a material amount of injury characteristic of.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Cutters usually have a rounded tip, are thin to medium in body, and.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.1165 — Lugs (X Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves normally grown near the bottom of the stalk. Leaves of the X group usually have a blunt tip and open face; they show some ground injury characteristic of the group.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Leaves of the P group ripen prematurely as a result of starvation and show a material amount of injury characteristic of leaves grown close to the ground.

creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture

description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Scrap accumulates from handling tobacco in farm buildings, warehouses, packing and conditioning plants, and stemmeries.

Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The application of these official standard grades shall be in accordance with the following rules.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2392 — Rule 1.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Each grade shall be treated as a subdivision of a particular type. When the grade is stated in an inspection certificate, the type also shall be stated.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2393 — Rule 2.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The determination of a grade shall be based upon a thorough examination of a lot of tobacco or of an official sample of the lot.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2394 — Rule 3.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). In drawing an official sample from a hogshead or other package of tobacco, two or more breaks shall be made at such points and in such manner as the inspector or sampler may find necessary to determine the kinds of tobacco and the percentage.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2396 — Rule 5.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The grade assigned to any lot of tobacco shall be a true representation of the tobacco at the time of inspection and certification. If, at any time, it is found that a lot of tobacco does not comply with the specifications of the grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2397 — Rule 6.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A lot of tobacco on the marginal line between two colors shall be placed in the color with which it best corresponds with respect to body or other associated elements of quality.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2398 — Rule 7.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of tobacco which meets the specifications of two grades shall be placed in the higher grade. Any lot of tobacco on the marginal line between two grades shall be placed in the lower grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2399 — Rule 8.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A lot of tobacco meets the specifications of a grade when it is not lower in any degree of any element of quality than the minimum specifications of such grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2400 — Rule 9.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). In determining the grade of a lot of tobacco, the lot as a whole shall be considered. Minor irregularities which do not affect over 1 percent of the tobacco shall be overlooked.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2401 — Rule 10.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any special factor symbol approved by the Director of the Tobacco Division, Agricultural Marketing Service, may be used after a grademark to show a peculiar side or characteristic of the tobacco which tends to modify the grade.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2402 — Rule 11.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Interpretations, the use of specifications, and the meaning of terms shall be in accordance with determinations or clarifications made by the Chief of the Standards and Testing Branch and approved by the Director.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2403 — Rule 12.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The use of any grade may be restricted by the Director during any marketing season, when it is found that the grade is not needed or appears in insufficient volume to justify its use.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2404 — Rule 13.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Length shall be stated in connection with each grade of the A, B and C groups and may be stated in connection with the grades of other groups. The standard tobacco sizes shall be used.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2405 — Rule 14.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The standard tobacco size 2 shall be used to designate X group tobacco of M or G color when such tobacco is 20 inches or over in length.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2406 — Rule 15.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Uniformity shall be expressed in percentages. These percentages shall govern the portion of a lot which must meet each specification of the grade. The minor portion must be closely related but may be of a different group, quality, and color from the major portion.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2407 — Rule 16.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Injury tolerance shall be expressed in percentages. The appraisal of injury shall be based upon the percentage of affected leaf surface or the degree of injury. In appraising injury, consideration shall be given to the normal characteristics of the group.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2408 — Rule 17.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of tobacco of the B, C, or X groups containing over 30 percent of mixed color or variegated leaves or over 30 percent of mixed color and variegated leaves combined shall be classified as “mixed” and designated by the color symbol “M.”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2409 — Rule 18.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any lot of tobacco containing 20 percent or more of green leaves or any lot which is not crude but contains 20 percent or more of green and crude combined shall be designated by the color symbols “G”, “GL”, or “GD”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2410 — Rule 19.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Crude leaves shall not be included in any grade of any color except green, light green, or dark green. Any lot containing 20 percent or more of crude leaves shall be designated nondescript.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2411 — Rule 20.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco damaged under 20 percent but which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a subgrade by placing the special factor “U” after the grademark. Tobacco damaged 20 percent or more shall be designated “No-G.”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2412 — Rule 21.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Sound tobacco that is wet or in doubtful-keeping order but which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a subgrade by placing the special factor “W” after the grademark. This special factor does not apply to tobacco designated “No-G.”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2413 — Rule 22.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco shall be designated No Grade, using the grademark “No-G,” when it is classified as dirty, nested, offtype, semicured, premature primings, damaged 20 percent or more, extremely wet or watered or when it needs to be reworked, contains foreign matter, or has an odor.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2414 — Rule 23.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco that is semifired but which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a subgrade by placing the special factor “SF” after the grademark. This factor does not apply to tobacco designated “No-G”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2436 — Wrappers (A Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves usually grown at or above the center portion of the stalk. Cured leaves of the A group show a low percentage of injury affecting wrapper yield. Wrappers are high in oil, very elastic, and have a smooth leaf surface.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2437 — Heavy Leaf (B Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves usually grown at or above the center portion of the stalk. These leaves have a pointed tip, tend to fold, are heavier in body than those of the X or C groups, and show no ground injury. Choice- and.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2438 — Thin Leaf (C Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves usually grown at the center portion of the stalk. These leaves normally have a rounded tip, are thinner in body than those of the B group, and show little or no ground injury. Choice- and fine-quality tobacco of this.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2439 — Lugs (X Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves that normally grow near the bottom of the stalk. These leaves usually have a blunt tip, tend to roll, and show ground injury.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2440 — (N Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Extremely common tobacco which does not meet the minimum specifications or which exceeds the tolerance of the lowest grade of any other group except scrap.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2441 — Scrap (S Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A byproduct of unstemmed and stemmed tobacco. Scrap accumulates from handling tobacco in farm buildings, warehouses, packing and conditioning plants, and stemmeries.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2461 — Summary of standard grades.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Special factors “U”, “W” and “SF” may be applied to all grades. Tobacco not covered by the standard grades is designated “No-G.”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2501 — Definitions.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). As used in these standards, the words and phrases hereinafter defined shall have the indicated meanings so assigned.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2502 — Air-dried.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The condition of unfermented tobacco as customarily prepared for storage under natural atmospheric conditions.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2503 — Body.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The thickness and density of a leaf or the weight per unit of surface. (See chart, § 29.2601.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2504 — Brown colors.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A group of colors ranging from a reddish brown to yellowish brown. These colors vary from low to medium saturation and from very low to medium brilliance. As used in these standards, the range is expressed as light brown (L), medium brown (F), and.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2505 — Class.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A major division of tobacco based on method of cure or principal usage.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2506 — Clean.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco is described as clean when it contains only a normal amount of sand or soil particles. Leaves grown on the lower portion of the stalk normally contain more dirt or sand than those from higher stalk positions. (See Rule 4, § 29.2620.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2507 — Color.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The third factor of a grade based on the relative hues, saturation or chroma, and color values common to the type.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2508 — Color intensity.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The varying degree of saturation or chroma. Color intensity as applied to tobacco describes the strength or weakness of a specific color or hue. It is applicable to brown colors. (See chart, § 29.2601.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2509 — Color symbols.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). As applied to these types, color symbols are L—light brown, F—medium brown, D—dark brown, M—mixed or variegated VF—greenish medium brown, and G—green.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2510 — Condition.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The state of tobacco which results from the method of preparation or from the degree of fermentation. Words used to describe the condition of tobacco are undried, air-dried, steam-dried, sweating, sweated, and aged.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2511 — Crude.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A subdegree of maturity. Crude leaves are usually hard and slick as a result of extreme immaturity. A similar condition may result from firekill, sunburn, or sunscald. Any leaf which is crude to the extent of 20 percent or more of its surface may.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2512 — Cured.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco dried of its sap by either natural or artificial processes.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2513 — Damage.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The effect of mold, must, rot, black rot, or other fungus or bacterial diseases which attack tobacco in its cured state. Tobacco having the odor of mold, must, or rot is considered damaged. (See Rule 20, § 29.2636.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2514 — Dirty.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The state of tobacco containing an abnormal amount of dirt or sand, or tobacco to which additional quantities of dirt or sand have been added. (See Rule 22, § 29.2638.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2515 — Elasticity.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The flexible, springy nature of the tobacco leaf to recover approximately its original size and shape after it has been stretched. (See chart, § 29.2601.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2516 — Elements of quality.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Physical characteristics used to determine the quality of tobacco. Words selected to describe degrees within each element are shown in the chart in § 29.2601.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2517 — Fiber.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The term applied to the veins in a tobacco leaf. The large central vein is called the midrib or stem. The smaller lateral and cross veins are considered from the standpoint of size and color.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2518 — Finish.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The reflectance factor in color perception. Finish indicates the sheen or shine of the surface of a tobacco leaf. (See chart, § 29.2601.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2519 — Fire-cured.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco cured under artificial atmospheric conditions by the use of open fires from which the smoke and fumes of burning wood are partly absorbed by the tobacco.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2520 — Foreign matter.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any extraneous substance or material such as stalks, suckers, straw, strings, rubber bands, and abnormal amounts of dirt or sand. (See Rule 22, § 29.2638.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2521 — Form.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The stage of preparation of tobacco such as unstemmed or stemmed.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2522 — Grade.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A subdivision of a type according to group, quality, and color.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2523 — Grademark.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A grademark normally consists of three symbols which indicate group, quality, and color. A letter is used to indicate group, a number to indicate quality, and a letter or letters to indicate color. For example, B3D means Heavy Leaf, good quality, and dark-brown color.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2524 — Green (G).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A term applied to green-colored tobacco. Any leaf which has a green color affecting 20 percent or more of its surface may be described as green. (See Rule 18, § 29.2634.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2525 — Greenish.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A term applied to greenish-tinged tobacco. Any leaf which has a greenish tinge or a pale green color affecting 20 percent or more of its surface may be described as greenish. (See Rule 17, § 29.2633.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2526 — Group.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A division of a type covering closely related grades based on certain characteristics which are usually related to stalk position, body, or the general quality of the tobacco. Groups in these types are Wrappers (A), Heavy Leaf (B), Thin Leaf (C), Lugs (X), Nondescript.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2527 — Injury.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Hurt or impairment from any cause except the fungous or bacterial diseases which attack tobacco in its cured state. (See Rule 15, § 29.2631.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2528 — Leaf.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Whole, unstemmed leaf. Leaf, when applied to tobacco in strip form, shall describe the divided unit of a whole leaf.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2529 — Leaf scrap.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture

description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco damaged under 20 percent but which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a subgrade by placing the special factor “U” after the grademark. Tobacco damaged 20 percent or more shall be designated “No-G.”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2637 — Rule 21.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Sound tobacco that is wet or in doubtful-keeping order but which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a subgrade by placing the special factor “W” after the grademark. This special factor does not apply to tobacco designated “No-G.”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2638 — Rule 22.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco shall be designated No Grade, using the grademark “No-G,” when it is dirty, nested, offtype, semicured, damaged 20 percent or more, extremely wet or watered, or when it needs to be reworked, contains foreign matter, or has an odor foreign to type.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2639 — Rule 23.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco in strip form which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a subgrade by placing the special factor “S” preceding the grademark.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2640 — Rule 24.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco that is semifired but which otherwise meets the specifications of a grade shall be treated as a subgrade by placing the special factor “SF” after the grademark. This factor does not apply to tobacco designated “No-G”.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2661 — Wrappers (A Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves usually grown at or above the center portion of the stalk. Cured leaves of this group are elastic and show a low percentage of injury affecting wrapper yield.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2662 — Heavy Leaf (B Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves which are medium to heavy in body.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2663 — Thin Leaf (C Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves that are thin in body.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2664 — Lugs (X Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). This group consists of leaves that normally grow near the bottom of the stalk. Leaves of the X group usually have a high degree of maturity and show ground injury.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2665 — Nondescript (N Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Extremely common tobacco which does not meet the minimum specifications or which exceeds the tolerance of the lowest grade of any other group except Scrap.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.2666 — Scrap (S Group).
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A byproduct of unstemmed and stemmed tobacco. Scrap accumulates from handling tobacco in farm buildings, warehouses, packing and conditioning plants, and stemmeries.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3001 — Definitions.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). As used in these standards, the words and phrases hereinafter defined shall have the indicated meanings so assigned.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3002 — Air-cured.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco cured under natural atmospheric conditions. Artificial heat is sometimes used to control excess humidity during the curing period to prevent house-burn and barn-burn in damp weather. Air-cured tobacco should not carry the odor of smoke or fumes resulting from the application of artificial.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3003 — Air-dried.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The condition of unfermented tobacco as customarily prepared for storage under natural atmospheric conditions.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3004 — Body.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The thickness and density of a leaf or the weight per unit of surface. (See Elements of quality.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3005 — Burley, Type 31.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). That type of air-cured tobacco, commonly known as Burley, produced principally in Kentucky, Tennessee, Virginia, North Carolina, Ohio, Indiana, West Virginia, and Missouri.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3006 — Burley, Type 93.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). That type of air-cured tobacco commonly known as Foreign-grown Burley, produced in countries other than the United States.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3008 — Class.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A major division of tobacco based on method of cure or principal usage.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3009 — Clean.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco is described as clean when it contains only a normal amount of sand or soil particles. Leaves grown on the lower portion of the stalk normally contain more dirt or sand than those from higher stalk positions. (See Rule 20.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3010 — Color.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The third factor of a grade, based on the relative hues, saturations or chroma, and color values common to the type.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3011 — Color intensity.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The varying degree of saturation or chroma. Color intensity as applied to tobacco describes the strength or weakness of a specific color or hue. It is applicable to all colors except variegated. Color intensity is reversed in its application to grades of greenish and.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3012 — Color symbols.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). As applied to Burley, single color symbols are as follows: L—buff, F—tan, R—red, D—dark red, K—variegated, M—mixed color, V—greenish, and G—green.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3013 — Combination color symbols.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). As applied to Burley, combination color symbols are as follows: FL—tannish buff, FR—tannish red, VF—greenish tan, VR—greenish red, GF—green tan, and GR—green red. (See rules 17 and 18.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3014 — Condition.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The state of tobacco which results from the method of preparation or from the degree of fermentation. Words used to describe the condition of tobacco are as follows: Undried, air-dried, steam-dried, sweating, sweated, and aged. Burley is air-dried or steam-dried for storage and aging.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3015 — Crude.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). A subdegree of maturity. Crude leaves are usually hard and slick as a result of extreme immaturity. A similar condition may result from sunburn or sunscald. Any leaf which is crude to the extent of 20 percent of its leaf surface may be described.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3016 — Cured.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: United States law. Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Tobacco dried of its sap by either natural or artificial processes.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3017 — Damage.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The effect of mold, must, rot, black rot, or other fungous or bacterial diseases which attack tobacco in its cured state. Tobacco having the odor of mold, must, or rot is considered damaged. (See Rule 23.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3019 — Dirty.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The state of tobacco containing an abnormal amount of dirt or sand, or tobacco to which additional quantities of dirt or sand have been added. (See Rule 23.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3020 — Elements of quality.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Elements of quality and the degrees used in the specifications of the official standard grades of Burley, Types 31 and 93, are shown in § 29.3101. Words have been selected to describe the degrees of each element. Some of the words are almost synonymous.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3021 — Fiber.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The term applied to the veins in a tobacco leaf. The large central vein is called the midrib or stem. The smaller lateral and cross veins are considered from the standpoint of size and color and in some types are treated as elements of.

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3022 — Finish.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). The reflectance factor in color perception. Finish indicates the sheen or shine of the surface of a tobacco leaf. Descriptive terms range from bright to dingy. (See Elements of quality.).

title: 7 C.F.R. § 29.3023 — Foreign matter.
creator: Agricultural Marketing Service (Standards, Inspections, Marketing Practices), Department Of Agriculture
description: Code of Federal Regulations, Title 7 (Agriculture), Part 29 (Tobacco Inspection). Text from the eCFR as of 2026-10-26 (unofficial editorial compilation; the official edition is the annual CFR). Any extraneous substance or material such as stalks, suckers, straw, strings, rubber bands, et cetera. Abnormal amounts of dirt or sand also are included. (See Rule 23.).
